domain: consumer product safety / cross-jurisdiction recall propagation prediction (OECD GlobalRecalls compilation)
prediction_question: The lead probed was the OECD GlobalRecalls portal (globalrecalls.oecd.org), the OECD Working Party on Consumer Product Safety's compilation of consumer product recalls contributed by ~47-50 national and regional authorities (launched 2012). The natural differentiated task was cross-jurisdiction propagation: at the portal publication of a product recall in jurisdiction A at instant T, will the same product be recalled in jurisdiction B within a fixed window? That is the one task shape this compilation could carry that no single national recalls portal can (in-house comparators hc-recalls-classification, openfda-food-recall-classification and rasff-notification-risk-decision are single-portal classification tasks on food/health products, not propagation). The session measured the source's coverage and closed the lead: the propagation target's negative class is censoring-dominated by heterogeneous contributor coverage, and the compilation adds no clean licence or unique access over the four reliably-contributing national portals.
prediction_time: Would have been the publication instant of the first-seen recall of a product in jurisdiction A (the portal's recall record date), with features from that record (product category via GS1 GPC, hazard, country of manufacture, description) - closed after aggregate measurement, before any full-schema or split work, because the target contract fails on measured coverage.
target_definition: Would have been binary: a later portal record for the same product in a different jurisdiction within N days, label source = a later recall record linked to the same product. Two blockers measured/verified: (1) no recorded second-jurisdiction recall cannot be read as absence, because contributor coverage is radically heterogeneous (measured: ~20 of 50 jurisdictions carry fewer than 100 lifetime notices; the OECD's own documentation states 'The scope of the recalls depends on the mandate of the particular government authority providing the information'); (2) the 4-row sample carries no product identity field (GTIN/model) beyond product.name and GS1 GPC category facets, which identify a category, not a product - the same-product link the label depends on is not visibly present in the public search payload.

sources.name: OECD GlobalRecalls portal (globalrecalls.oecd.org), consumer product recalls contributed by national/regional authorities
sources.api: No documented public read API. The SPA (Angular shell, main.b95c2851e3e9cc7b2275.js, fetched 2026-10-31) calls an anonymous MarkLogic web service at https://globalrecalls.oecd.org/ws/ (search.xqy?q=&start=&end=&lang=; getrecall.xqy?uri=; mainDashboards.xqy?q=&lang=; getproductstaxonomy.xqy; rss.xqy), plus /ws/import.xqy?apikey (contributor uploads) and /ws/export.xqy exposed only in the admin area. The only API the OECD documents for this portal is the contributor upload API (API keys issued to contributing agencies; OECD GlobalRecalls portal: 2015-2019 enhancements, https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-globalrecalls-portal_d8b0d605-en.html). Search results are returned by the ws endpoint with a copyright field: '© OECD. All rights reserved - http://www.oecd.org/termsandconditions'.
sources.license: No dataset-level open licence found anywhere on the portal; the OECD general Terms and Conditions Data section (updated 1 July 2024, https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, fetched 2026-10-31) permits reuse of OECD-owned Data with attribution but is explicitly conditional on third-party ownership being cleared by the user.

license_evidence: OECD Terms & Conditions (updated 1 July 2024), https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, fetched 2026-10-31, section 3 (Data): 'Data may be subject to restrictions beyond the scope of these Terms and Conditions, either because specific terms apply to those Data or because third parties may have ownership interests. It is the user's responsibility to verify, either directly in the metadata or ... by ... referring to the "source" tab, whether the Data is fully or partially owned by third parties and/or whether additional restrictions may apply, and to contact the owner of the Data before incorporating it in your work in order to secure the necessary permissions.' and 'The OECD in no way represents or warrants that it owns or controls all rights in all Data.' - GlobalRecalls rows are contributed by ~50 national/regional recall authorities, so a derived whole-portal dataset needs per-jurisdiction permission clearance; the compilation layer alone is not a grant over the rows.

The portal's own search endpoint response embeds: '© OECD. All rights reserved - http://www.oecd.org/termsandconditions' (measured 2026-10-31, see notes.md) - no open-licence string is served with the data anywhere on the portal.

OECD GlobalRecalls portal: 2015-2019 enhancements (OECD, 2020), https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2020/05/oecd-globalrecalls-portal_a4bf1196/d8b0d605-en.pdf (read 2026-10-31 via live-PDF extraction): API keys are issued to contributing agencies to PUSH recall zip files into the portal; jurisdictions upload manually or automatically at their own technological capacity - i.e. the documented API is a contributor ingestion channel, not a public read channel.

OECD Statistics and Data Outputs 2024 (https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/data/methods/oecd-statistics-and-data-outputs/OECD-Statistics-and-Data-Outputs.pdf, read 2026-10-31 via live-PDF extraction): 'The GlobalRecalls portal brings together information on mandatory and voluntary consumer product recalls and safety warnings issued by, or notified to, a government authority and made publicly available. The scope of the recalls depends on the mandate of the particular government authority providing the information.' - the publisher's own statement that record absence is coverage-dependent.
split_strategy: Not reached - the aggregate coverage measurement (below) closed the lead before split work. For the propagation target, split capacity is not the binding failure: the target itself is uninterpretable at the measured coverage mix (negatives are censoring-dominated; the four reliably-contributing channels - US CPSC, Canada, Australia, EU Safety Gate - are exactly the national portals a consumer can already download, and EU Safety Gate natively publishes follow-up alerts by member states, covering the EU part of the propagation signal).

measurements.portal_aggregates_2026_10_31: Two anonymous GETs to the SPA's own dashboard/search endpoints (the calls the public UI issues on load; no bulk transfer, 16,806 B + 246,490 B): Total recalls 57,807; country facet lists 50 jurisdictions; measured mix (reproduced by probe/probe_aggregates.py): EEA 15,002 / US 8,421 / AU 6,620 / CA 5,759 / DE 4,507 / IT 3,403 / GB 3,245 / KR 2,976 / HU 2,754 / FR 2,585 / CZ 1,363 / PL 1,350 / ES 1,230 / CY 1,076 / JP 1,063 / SE 1,060 / FI 1,054 / BG 993 / LT 863 / NL 767 / CO 699 / SK 640 / IE 510 / DK 494 / RO 473 / BE 442 / PT 416 / AT 355 / AE 289 / ASEAN 275 / LV 274 / GR 268 / MT 257 / LU 255 / HR 214 / EE 211 / NO 172 / SI 167 / VN 89 / PH 82 / SG 70 / IS 69 / ID 67 / CR 54 / TW 47 / TH 33 / BN 31 / IL 19 / MY 19 / LI 1. Top-5 channels hold 40,309 of 57,807 (69.7%); 12 of the 50 jurisdictions hold fewer than 100 lifetime notices (Liechtenstein holds 1). Facet keys measured: country-were-recalled, country-were-made, gs1-gpc-brick/class/family/segment, concepts-from-query, best-tags, related-concepts.
measurements.sample_rows_2026_10_31: search.xqy sample (start=1&end=5, orderby date-asc) returned 4 rows; fields measured: countryId, countryName, date, extUrl (link to the originating national portal record), id, imageUri, index, language, languageId, manufacturer.country, product.name, tags, uri, plus a url field pointing at an INTERNAL OECD hostname (dmz-ml-2.main.oecd.org:8120/service/getrecall.xqy) for the detail. No GTIN/model/product-identity field in the payload; the GS1 GPC facets are category-level. Data-quality signal: 2 of the 4 sample rows carry date 1900-01-01, i.e. a missing/unparsed date sentinel in a timing-critical field (reproduced by probe/probe_aggregates.py).
measurements.task_probes_deliberately_not_run: No full-schema crawl, no year-distribution extraction, no product-linkage probe, no split or cost measurement - the coverage mix plus the publisher's own scope caveat settled the target contract, and the licence posture settled publishability, so further probing would spend budget on a closed lead. Cost of this rejection: 4 HTTP fetches to the portal + 1 OECD report PDF + 1 OECD statistics PDF + 1 OECD ToU page.

rejection_reason: Two decisive grounds. (1) Target contract: the only differentiated task this compilation can carry is cross-jurisdiction propagation, and its negative class requires reading 'no second-jurisdiction recall recorded' as absence of one. Measured coverage makes that censoring-dominated: 57,807 notices total across 50 jurisdictions, top-5 channels hold 69.7% (40,309), and 12 of the 50 jurisdictions carry fewer than 100 lifetime notices (Liechtenstein 1, Malaysia 19, Israel 19); the OECD itself states the scope of contributed recalls 'depends on the mandate of the particular government authority providing the information', and its implementation history documents contributors joining gradually (manual uploads, pre-production systems). A propagation label over this mix measures contributor activity as much as product risk. The sample payload also carries no product-identity field (name + GPC category only), so the same-product linkage the label needs is not present in the public search response. (2) Publishability and contribution: no dataset-level open licence exists on the portal; the API serves an 'All rights reserved' line and the OECD's general Data permission explicitly excludes third-party-owned data from its grant, putting per-jurisdiction clearance on the user (class C: compilation of ~50 national owners with unstated-to-restrictive terms). Restricting the task to the reliably-contributing channels (US/CA/AU/EU Safety Gate) would fix coverage but makes the OECD layer redundant: those portals are directly downloadable by any consumer, and EU Safety Gate already natively publishes follow-up alerts by member state - the EU portion of the propagation signal is already a publisher product. Closed under the standing policy (unresolved class C), with the task-side negative finding recorded alongside it.
next_action: None - closed. Re-open only if (a) the OECD publishes a documented public read API or bulk export for GlobalRecalls AND an explicit dataset-level open licence covering the compilation, and (b) the record payload gains a product-identity field (GTIN/model) so same-product linkage is measurable, and (c) the task is scoped to the homogeneous auto-push channels with the censoring documented - which still leaves the source largely redundant with the national portals, so (c) alone is not sufficient. A national-portal propagation task scoped to EU Safety Gate follow-up alerts would be a separate EC-region candidate, not this one.

jurisdiction.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), headquartered in Paris, France
jurisdiction.convention: The publisher's HQ country is recorded because 'international' is not a country; the OECD is an intergovernmental organisation headquartered in Paris. The rows themselves are contributed by ~50 national/regional recall authorities, each a distinct jurisdiction (recorded because any licence path for a derived dataset runs per contributing authority, not through the OECD compilation alone). This candidate is in this session's assigned region (international organisations) and its jurisdiction is non-US.

licence_note: Class C (unstated/ambiguous for the rows): the OECD's general Data permission (Terms & Conditions updated 1 July 2024) grants reuse of OECD-owned data with attribution, but explicitly conditions it on the user verifying and clearing third-party ownership; GlobalRecalls rows are contributed by national/regional authorities and the portal serves '© OECD. All rights reserved' with no dataset-level open licence. No candidate-specific operator risk acceptance exists, so the standing class C policy closes the lead.
